def quote_each_word(s):
    """Hey — quick one for you! Picture a tiny display widget where every
    word needs its own little pair of quotes around it. That's the entire
    gig here.

    The setup:
    - s contains words separated by single spaces (never two spaces in a row); s may be empty.
    - Return s with every word wrapped in double-quote characters, words still separated by single spaces; the empty string stays empty.

    Honestly, that's the whole job — one of those functions that takes
    longer to read about than to write. Enjoy!

    >>> quote_each_word('')
    ''
    >>> quote_each_word('a b')
    '"a" "b"'
    """
